utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand that we will hear from Mr. Vujanovic -- we are not ready yet, Mr. Marro -- and that you will hear regarding Mr. Budimir's presence either via video link or coming to The Hague at noon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So we thought we would hear Mr. Vujanovic and, depending upon when we finish, then stand in recess until 1.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But I do not know how long we need for Mr. Vujanovic. Was it just cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have any idea how long you will need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think that schedule will work out fine.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: An hour or so?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do not think it will be any longer than that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I thought an hour without even remembering the testimony. OK, so if we then finish up at maybe 11.30 or quarter to 12, as long as we have an hour and a half recess, then we would stand in recess until 1.30. Let us see. Mr. Marro, would you bring in Mr. Vujanovic, please? ^^ MIRKO VUJANOVIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, you understand that you are still under the oath that you took when you last testified to tell the truth, do you not? Mr. Vujanovic, can you hear me? Mr. Vujanovic, you are still under the oath that you took when you last testified to tell the truth. Do you understand that? Mr. Marro -- Mr. Vujanovic, can you hear me? Mr. Vujanovic, you are still under the oath that you took when you last testified to tell the truth. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vujanovic, during your previous testimony ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- you discussed the register or timetable of shifts which you prepared, and explained to us how that document was supposed to be prepared. As I understand it, you would obtain your information from a daily schedule which was prepared by the station Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That daily schedule was prepared a day before the shifts were actually supposed to work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then after the scheduled shift ----

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just, please, we have no transcript. Would you mind to stop just a little moment, please, because it is very difficult to follow? If you could just stop for a few seconds?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: Oh, it is working. Thank you very much. It is now working.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How much have you missed or what is the last entry that you have on your transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARRO
utterances.text: None. We have none. We have none until now.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Then we will begin again. Mr. Tieger, would you begin, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, because the earlier questions and answers did not appear on the written transcript, I am going to ask you those questions once more. The information ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- which you used to prepare the timetable of shifts or register of shifts was obtained from a daily schedule which was prepared by the station Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That daily schedule was prepared the day before the shifts were actually supposed to work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the scheduled shift, the shift leader was supposed to report to the station Commander if someone had missed the shift, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Any change would be entered in the timetable.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: By the "timetable" you mean the daily schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the daily schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then that daily schedule was passed on to you and you entered the information the day after the scheduled shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The daily schedule was supposed to be thrown out or discarded after a period of time and probably not more than two years, I believe you indicated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The timetable or register of shifts which you prepared was preserved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the work list was preserved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, and by "work list" you are referring to the document which you prepared and which you discussed in your earlier testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For clarification, I will continue to call that a work list and that is the document which you prepared on the basis of the daily schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This Court heard from major of police, Djuro Prpos, that there is an official duty plan that was prepared by or under the authority of the Commander. Are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Djuro worked in a different station and I do not know what kind of a timetable they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the Commander of your station prepared an official duty plan which was contained in a book and which was preserved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think that he would only make a draft, and then on the basis of that draft a daily schedule was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You are not familiar with any book known as Raspored Sluzbe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know one way or another whether the Commander of your station prepared a document for his own purposes or for other record keeping purposes from which the daily timetable or the daily schedule was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I kept the records that I am familiar with. As far as other records are concerned, whether they kept them for their own purposes, for their own personal needs, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So in your particular case, you did not have access to any document from which the daily schedule might have been taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I would only get the daily schedule as it was prepared, and then after the duty was performed I would simply enter this into the work list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that daily schedule posted anywhere in the station, for example, on a bulletin board so that police officers would know what their next duty assignment was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The daily timetable after having been written by the Commander and signed by the Commander is given to the shift leader and then it is there in the duty station and then the policemen come in and see whatever may be of interest to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We also heard from Mr. Prpos and from other officers that there are duty reports or patrol reports which are prepared by the officers engaged in that particular patrol or by the shift leader. Are you aware of those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Such documents existed only in the case of extraordinary affairs conducted by the police, but there are no patrol orders within the regular police affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For record keeping purposes, they would not be submitted to you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to receive such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But you are aware that such documents existed and were prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Specifically in this period during which I worked, no, I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You are aware of duty reports in general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In general, you are aware that there are reports, duty reports or patrol reports, which are filled out by shift leaders or officers in the field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know that there are patrol reports or patrol orders. I am not aware of duty reports or work reports or work orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The patrol reports or patrol orders or patrol warrants contain information such as the duty to be performed, what happened on the shift, at what times those things happened, where they occurred and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is part of the patrol reports. After the duty performed and after regular service, then there are reports that are filed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, let me ask you at this point to look for a moment at Exhibit 74A, the August 1992 work list. You now have that document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at August 21st on that work list, it indicates that Dusko Tadic was working out of Prijedor station 1 on patrol 4, which was the area of the bus and railway station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the shift from ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That information was taken from the daily schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Its accuracy depends on whether the shift leader accurately reported whether Mr. Tadic was there, assuming that the shift Commander accurately conveyed that information on the schedule and assuming that it was all written down accurately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the entire procedure is completed, then I enter this into the work list on the basis of the daily schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Its accuracy depends on some of the factors I just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point may the witness be presented with a document, a copy of which is present in Banja Luka and which is marked PA1? The translation is PA2.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have that, Miss de Bertodano, Mr. Kay? You do have that in front of you PA1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not as supplied, but we do have a copy of the particular document that is going to be produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like that marked for identification as Prosecution 356. Mr. Vujanovic, I do not know if other daily schedules have survived, but this is a document which was provided to the Prosecution by the Defence and which they explained they received from the Prijedor police. This document states in the upper right-hand corner that it is page 5 of the daily schedule of shifts for Prijedor station 1 for August 21st 1992, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of this timetable I cannot -- I mean, I have to look at the work list that I kept also. I have to compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We will be doing that in just a moment, sir. But this appears to be the daily schedule for August 21st, 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it says here, but I cannot before seeing the work list, it is only on that basis that I can draw a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This document bears the stamp of Republika Srpska, Banja Luka security service, Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Prosecution 356 will be admitted. A will be in Serbo-Croatian and B the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have a copy of the translation as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We have copies for the Court. I am just passing out copies to the Court at the moment, Mr. Vujanovic. Mr. Vujanovic, can you still hear me? Mr. Vujanovic, the policemen on this daily schedule for sector 4 are listed in three different groups of eight or seven, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Those groups represent the three different shifts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the top of the page in the first above those columns the times of the shifts are listed? At the far left 6 to 1400, in the middle the 14 to 2100 shift and in the right the 2100 to 6.00 a.m. shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the time spent on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at the 1400 to 2100 shift for August 21st, who was the third policeman listed for group 4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I have not quite understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sure. For sector 4, the railway and bus station area, who was the third policeman listed for the 1400 to 2100 shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The third policeman is Tadic, Dusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember the time which appeared for Dusko Tadic for August 21st on the August work list which you prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to have a look at it, if possible. If I can have a look at an excerpt from the work list, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please. It is Exhibit 74A. Now that you are looking at the work list, Mr. Vujanovic, which shift does it show that Dusko Tadic worked on on August 21st?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 21st August it says that he worked in the fourth sector from 6 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the work list says he worked from 6 to 1400 hours and the daily schedule for the same day says he worked from 1400 to 2100 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to this information here, if you look at the right-hand box on the top, this was written in subsequently because regularly it is not entered as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was written subsequently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We attach the fifth page of the daily timetable of services in the police station of August 21st 1992 with the remark that daily timetables of the police employees were -- and the rest is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. That is a note from the police station indicating what this document is. That is the Prijedor police station saying that this is ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who signed this document, I mean, who wrote in -- wrote this in subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I appreciate that, sir, but this is the document which was provided by the Prijedor police station as the daily schedule, as a copy of the daily schedule, for August 21st 1992, bearing the stamp of the police station for Republika Srpska, Banja Luka security services, Prijedor station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also there is a stamp, a seal, at the bottom of the page where the Commander signed this daily schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you do not know who is responsible for the discrepancy between the two, sir -- you or the person who provided this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most probably it is a technical error, a typographical error when it was typed out, the schedule. Perhaps it is 12th August 1992, because if you look at the date of 12th of this same month it says that Tadic worked in sector 4 from 14 to 2100 hours. So, probably it is a technical error when it was typed out because the schedule that is signed by the Commander has to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Certainly there is no possibility of any human error in transcribing these things or any purposeful change of the schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so; only perhaps a technical error when typing it out, the Secretary who typed this out, the typist.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, let us move on for a moment then to Exhibit 78A, the September work list. Do you have that document in front of you now, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This document indicates that on September 1st Dusko Tadic worked at patrol 4, the railway and bus station area, on the 600 to 1400 hour shift. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, which Exhibit is this now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 78A, your Honour. [To the witness]: The same shift on September 2nd, at the same place. The 2100 to 600 hour shift on September 3rd to the morning of September 4th at the same place. Then on the 5th ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a break in the link so I did not quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am just trying to run quickly through the information shown on the work list. I had mentioned that on September 2nd the work list indicates that he worked at sector 4 on the 600 to 1400 hour shift; that on 3rd September he worked ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: --- again at the railway and bus station area on the 2100 hour shift which began on September 3rd to 600 hours on September 4th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On the 4th from 2100 to 600?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On 5th he did not show up to work, although he was scheduled to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the previous shift, he should have been working from 14 to 2100 hours but he did not work that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. Then so on until through 8th and until 9th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Those were all at the railway and bus station area in central Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For Prijedor station 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Police station Prijedor 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again all that information is supposed to show where Dusko Tadic was, assuming that the shift leader accurately reported his presence or absence, that the shift Commander accurately recorded it on the daily schedule or reported it to you and assuming that it was accurately recorded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The shift leader's duty was to inform the station Commander of any change which the Commander would take over from the shift leader every morning when he came to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was one of the factors on which the accuracy of the work list was dependent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have a number of documents marked as the next Prosecution Exhibit for identification. Those documents in Banja Luka and here have been marked as PC1 and 1A, PC2. The translations are marked as PC4, PC5, PC6 and PC7. I mention that both for the benefit of the persons in Banja Luka and also so the Court will understand the notations on these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of those, Miss de Bertodano?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I believe I do, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Those then will be marked as -- what Prosecution Exhibit then, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could have copies anyway just so I can check that the documents I have in front of me are the ones Mr. Tieger is referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When those are tendered and marked for identification purposes, then the usher -- he can actually show them to you first. Do you have a copy of those, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we do. For the Registrar's purposes, it might be best to indicate PC1, PC1A and PC2 as 357A, and PC4 through 7 which are the translations as 357B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss de Bertodano, are you marking on the copy that the usher gave you to look at?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I thought that was a copy for the Defence, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I thought it was going to be marked. Is there another copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, there is, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be then marked for identification purposes as Prosecution 357A and then B will be the translation. You may proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. [To the witness]: Could PC1, the page which has that reference, be presented to the witness, please? In fact, let us show the witness PC1, 1A and PC2. Mr. Vujanovic, these are also documents which were provided to the Prosecution by the Defence and which we were advised by them they received from the Prijedor police. You can see marked on those documents that they are from the Ministry of the Interior for the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, security services Banja Luka, and they bear the stamp of Republika Srpska, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender these for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 357A and B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, these are the patrol reports or patrol warrants of the type we discussed earlier, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to the page which is marked "PC1". Let us look at the report which is on the left side. This is a patrol report or a patrol warrant for a group which worked on September 1st, 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This patrol orders something I am not familiar with. They do not belong to the police station Prijedor 1 and, as far as I can see, they belong to the Kozarac police station, so that I am not familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just looking at the document, sir, you can see that it indicates a patrol for September 1st 1992?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, with regard to the admission of these documents, having said that there was no objection, it seems that these cannot be admitted through this witness because he has never seen them before.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, would you take your earphones off, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Go ahead, Miss de Bertodano.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears from the witness's answers to the previous questions that he has not seen these documents before, that he has had no connection with them, that they, in fact, come from another police station and, therefore, they cannot be admitted through this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a rather extraordinary objection, not only in terms of its timing, but in terms of its content. These are documents which were provided to the Prosecution by the Defence and which they represented to us had come from the Prijedor police and for which they had seen the originals. The Court will recall very early in this trial documents were admitted on the very basis of that representation by the Defence. I refer specifically to the mobilization list which was introduced and admitted quite some time ago and presented to a witness who knew nothing about it. But based on those representations by the Defence, the document was, in fact, admitted. This is a document for which a foundation has been laid, and that is that it came from the Prijedor police, the same organisation which provided the documents which have been the subject of some discussion for several days this week. Any objection about this witness's knowledge or lack of knowledge could only go to the weight to be given this document as well as the other documents. I have no problem with the argument that, in so far as all these documents are concerned, there may be a serious question about the weight, but clearly this particular document or this particular set of documents provided by the Prijedor police shed light on the weight to be given the other documents.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might just respond to that? The mobilization lists to which Mr. Tieger referred were presented through an expert witness to comment on the lists. That is a quite different situation from a witness of fact commenting on something which he has never, in fact, seen before. I am not objecting in principle to these documents, but only to the fact that they cannot be brought in through this witness because he cannot comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may say, they are not being brought in through this witness, they are being presented to this witness and brought into the foundation laid by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I will overrule your objection. It will go to the weight. 357A and B are still in. The only problem that you will have, of course, since he did not prepare these entries, I do not know how you are going to impeach any prior testimony or whatever that he may have given. I do not know what your intent was, but in any case let us see where you are going. Mr. Vujanovic, thank you. Mr. Vujanovic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, looking again at the patrol report on the left side of the page of PC1, that indicates, does it not, that it is a patrol report for a shift of September 1st 1992? Is that right, sir? I did not hear any answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not understood the question. Would you please be so kind as to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Certainly. I am directing your attention to the patrol report on the left side of the page and simply asking whether it indicates that is a patrol for September 1st 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It appears we have lost the sound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The sound was lost.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, would you please repeat your answer? We did not have the sound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I am working on these things and I know of such documents, patrol instructions and so on, but these documents that I have before me I am not familiar with, nor am I competent or authorised to provide any kind of information regarding those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me quickly direct your attention then to the page marked "PC2". On the left side of the page we see a patrol report. The date on that patrol report on this document is September 3rd 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: September 3rd 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The hours indicated are 17.30 to 600?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 17 to 600.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the area of Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is what the document says, however, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not even know whether Vidovici exists in that region there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The particular duty is reconnaissance duty; that is listed at the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The leader of the patrol of a total of six people is Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So this document shows Dusko Tadic patrolling in Vidovici, whether or not it exists, at the same time that your work list has him working at the bus and railway station in central Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could I please receive an extract from the work list?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please, that is 78A. What time does your work list, Exhibit 78A, say that Dusko Tadic was working at the railway and bus station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On September 3rd he worked from 21 to 6 hours in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: According to the work list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is all I have.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss de Bertodano?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, if I could take you back to the daily schedule which was marked Prosecution 356, and if a copy of that could be put in front of you? If we look at the note in the top right-hand corner, you told us that you thought that would have been written on later, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the regular daily schedule does not include any such remarks, so this was written in later.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You cannot see who has signed that part at the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to this signature, I cannot tell who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You also pointed out that there was another stamp at the bottom right-hand side of the page. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would that stamp normally be on a daily schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the lower right-hand corner it is normal and not in the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would the schedule normally be signed by someone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The daily schedule is signed by the station Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you see a signature of that sort on that daily schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the copy is highly illegible I cannot tell whose signature it is.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: But do you see that there is a signature there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: In your evidence you suggested that there might be a confusion between 21st and 12th August, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the schedule for the date of 21st, it says that Dusko Tadic was working from 6 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, I am afraid we lost some sound there so I am going to ask you to repeat your previous answer. I had asked you about the possible confusion between 12th and 21st August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A technical error in typing was probably made; instead of "12" the typist typed "21" because, according to the date, the 12th, it appears that Dusko Tadic worked from 9 to 21 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to some other names on that list. Could you look at the 14 to 21 hour shift at the fourth police region and the person listed at No. 5? Can you read out what you can of his name there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Boro.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you see a first letter of the surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first letter is a P or an R.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If I could ask for Exhibit 74A to be put in front of you again. If I could draw your attention to the name at 320 on that list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is the name there, so far as you can read it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Boro.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Again can you read an initial for the surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: P.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If you go along the schedule against that name to 12th August, can you tell me when and where this person was working on 12th August from that duty list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of this work list and the daily schedule, it emerges that this person worked with Dusko Tadic in the Fourth District.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What hours was he working according to the duty list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 1400 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If you could look along a few boxes to his entry for 21st August, what hours was he working on 21st August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Does the question refer to Boro?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 21st August he worked in the Fourth District from 6.00 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go back to the daily schedule and if you would look again with regard to the Fourth Police Region, the shift from 2100 hours to 06 hours, and the seventh name listed on that shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simo.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you read the first letter of the surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: S.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On Exhibit 74, the August duty book, can I ask you to look at the name at 321?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is the name written there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Simo" it says.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Again can you read the initial of the surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also S.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If you look along his duty shifts to his shift on 12th August, can you tell us what shift he was performing on that day, according to the duty list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of the list, he was working from 2100 to 06 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is that the same time as he is listed as working on the daily schedule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If we look along to 21st August on the duty list, what hours is he listed as working on 21st August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the person under 7, under No. 7?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Yes, but I am asking you with regard to the August '92 duty list where he is at No. 321.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For August 21st he worked in the Fourth District from 1400 to 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could get you to turn back to the daily schedule and look at one more name. In the Fifth Police Region on the 1400 to 2100 hours shift, could you read me the name that you see at No. 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It applies to the Fifth Police District.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: That is right, yes, 1400 to 2100-hour shift, and the name No. 3 on that shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you read the first initial of the surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: S.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I think you may be reading at No. 4. If I could ask you to look at No. 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the period from 1400 to 2100 hours?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Yes, at No. 3 in the Fifth Police Region.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miroslav?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Yes, and the initial of the surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: C.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: C.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If we look to the August 1992 duty list and we look to No. 318 on that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you read the name that appears there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: And the initial of the surname, if you can see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it, C.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If we look along his hours for August to 12th August, can you tell us what hours he was working on 12th August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 12th August he was working from 1400 to 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If we look further along to 21st August, what hours was he working on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 21st August, from 6 to 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those Exhibits can now be returned to the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have additional -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I had not finished, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am just rushing you right along! I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: (To the witness): You were shown by Mr. Tieger some patrol warrants and you told us that you were not familiar with these warrants, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were you familiar with anything that happened at Kozarac police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you know who wrote those warrants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you say whether they are genuine or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: However, the records that you have shown us from Prijedor police station are based on a system, as you have outlined to us, and a system which you had worked at regularly during 1992, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Vujanovic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, there is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujanovic, you are free to leave. However, you are not permanently excused. You may be recalled for testimony. So, please keep in touch with Mr. Wladimiroff and, if it is necessary for you to return to give additional testimony before the Tribunal, we will tell you. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is no problem whatsoever. If necessary I will be there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vujanovic. You are now excused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Well, the timing worked well. It is 10 minutes to 12.00. I understand you will hear something regarding Mr. Budimir at 12.00. We will stand in recess for lunch, but if you will let us now what you hear we will be here in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I heard slightly earlier that it would be 1.00 or after 1.00 o'clock from the Registry. Miss Featherstone had spoken directly to Mr. Marro.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Bos told me 12.00. Where are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let them fight it out!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is OK. You spoke last to Mr. Marro.

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: I did, yes. He said 1.00 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He said 1.00 o'clock. Does that pose a problem? We could still begin at 1.30. We will either begin with Mr. Budimir testifying via video link or we will not hear any more testimony, as I understand it, this afternoon since you do not have any more witnesses. They are coming this weekend and then Mr. Budimir would come next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So 1.30 will work, if you hear at 1.00. If you do not hear, of course, then we will be here and we will see whether we will actually begin at 1.30 or whether we will have a delay of waiting for a response. We do not want to lose too much time because you have listed Mr. Budimir for three hours and we do not want to wait too long. If we have not heard it would be better for Mr. Budimir to be there available rather than to lose that time and then have to use it next week, because next week is pretty full. We will stand in recess until 1.30.
